A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HS-STaR research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments across multiple backbones, including benchmark comparisons, difficulty-estimation analyses, and sampling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds threshold-sensitivity results in Section 4.6 and Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same reward-guided difficulty classification, boundary-focused budget reallocation, preference-pair construction, and DPO objective. The added threshold experiments do not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training remains based on MATH and NuminaMath-1.5. Evaluation retains GSM8K, MATH500, OlympiadBench, Minerva-Math, AMC23, College-Math, and AIME24. The zero-training scenario and cross-model difficulty-estimation evaluation already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same comparators, including vanilla SFT, stepwise initialization, STaR-RFT, STaR-DPO, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, SimpleRL, PURE-VR, and DPO-VP. Existing difficulty-estimation and re-sampling comparison variants are also retained.

E3.justification: The new threshold experiment evaluates (tau_l, tau_h) settings of (0.4, 0.6) and (0.2, 0.8), alongside the standard configuration, and measures boundary-detection precision and recall against SDE labels. Previously reported training settings and benchmark evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing how threshold ranges affect boundary identification and downstream performance. Earlier estimation, pre-sampling, and re-sampling analyses remain; the cross-model generalization analysis moves from Appendix D.2 into Section 4.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added threshold table uses point estimates. Three training iterations and Avg@32 evaluation were already reported in v1.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports precision/recall/average scores of 81.6/67.8/47.0 for narrower thresholds, 52.9/92.5/46.6 for broader thresholds, and 77.1/73.8/47.5 for the standard setting. Existing matched benchmark and ablation results remain unchanged; these are additional sensitivity results.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4, the formal difficulty categories, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added. The new precision and recall descriptions explain standard evaluation metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: boundary-level problems offer high learning utility, and reward-guided hierarchical sampling improves self-training under a fixed sampling budget. The added analysis supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 adds an interpretation linking threshold selection to precision, recall, sampling concentration, and boundary-example diversity. It also states that calibration can be reused across policy models for a fixed PRM. The existing applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents pilot-based threshold calibration, describes it as a one-time cost per PRM, and supplies the alternative threshold values tested. Existing appendix implementation settings, pseudocode, and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including Liu et al. on R1-Zero-like training, Fu et al. on RLAE, and Tian et al. on VC Search. These extend background citations without substantially changing the paper's positioning against response-focused or difficulty-aware prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording, terminology, affiliation, and contact-information edits. It inserts a threshold-analysis subsection and integrates the former Appendix D.2 discussion into Section 4.4, while retaining the overall narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4, moves v1 Figure 7 into the main text as Figure 4, and rearranges existing displays. It corrects the reversed inlier/outlier SDE ranges in the legends of Figures 3 and 4. Existing plotted values are retained.

improvement.justification: The new threshold study provides useful empirical support for parameter selection, and corrected difficulty legends remove misleading labels. These improve support and clarity without changing the central method or results. The pre-existing inconsistent threshold assignments between Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2 remain unresolved.
